A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete 25-page contents, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical experiments on MDPR and split-CIFAR10/100, including computed generalization bounds in Tables 1–3, plus a two-task simulation.

after.justification: v2 retains the original MDPR and split-CIFAR10/100 results in Tables 1–3 and the two-task simulation in Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: Appendix A newly describes an optional prior-conditioned posterior Q_i(P). Appendix C.2 also corrects the documented MDPR training loss to log(1+exp(-y w^T x)) and the bias update to the average of task means. These are limited formulation revisions; the PDFs do not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 953-task MDPR binary-classification dataset, its simplicity variants, split-CIFAR10/100 and the two-task toy simulation. No dataset, task or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same standard-rate and minimum-sample-size fast-rate baselines, MDPR oracle comparisons and CIFAR joint-constraint results. Oracle curves appearing in v2's main figures already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: MDPR training is specified as logistic regression in v2 Appendix C.2, replacing linear regression and its malformed loss expression in v1 Appendix B.2. This revises the reported training setting without establishing a rerun. Splits, optimization budgets, hyperparameters and CIFAR configurations are retained.

E4.justification: The two-task constraint-geometry simulation, Catoni-parameter comparisons, joint-constraint analysis, MDPR simplicity sweep and oracle comparisons are retained. Moving their plots into the main text introduces no additional analysis.

E5.justification: MDPR Tables 2–3 retain identical plus-or-minus reporting. No repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical entries and uncertainty values; for example, the task-centric CIFAR10 kl-style bound remains 0.272. The plotted trends and qualitative experimental findings are also unchanged after matching relocated figures.

T1.justification: v2 makes local mathematical repairs: Phi_a uses e^(-a) instead of e^(-1), the standard-rate proof specifies a finite union-bound grid, and the task-centric proof replaces log(sum 2sqrt(m_i)) with sum log(2sqrt(m_i)). The inverse Catoni definition gains its missing maximization objective and empirical-loss term (v1 Equation 90; v2 Equation 92). The principal bounds and proof strategies remain.

C1.justification: Both versions claim fast-rate bounds for unbalanced task-centric and sample-centric learning, limitations of balanced-setting proofs, and extensions to meta-learning. Adding 'PAC-Bayesian' to the abstract makes the already-established scope explicit.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explains why separate single-task bounds fail to exploit shared complexity and discusses potentially smaller KL terms versus additional adaptation costs for prior-conditioned posteriors. Existing experimental interpretations and the conclusion's limitations concerning interpretability and numerical optimization remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access footnote for the neural-network experiments in Appendix C.3 and corrects implementation formulas in C.2. SLSQP, JAX/Optax, optimization steps and hyperparameters were already documented in v1; their restatement is not new disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds Scott et al. (2024), Kraft (1988) and Yousefi et al. (2018). Section 3.1 additionally relates the minimum-sample-size bottleneck to PAC bounds. These modestly expand context while retaining the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and terminology, presents existing background bounds as numbered theorems, adds explanatory Appendix A, and improves proof cross-references and subsection organization. Most prose and the main narrative sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v1's detailed appendix Figures 3–4 become v2's main Figures 1–2, replacing the smaller combined display. Table 1 changes from a text-wrapped placement to a separate centered display. Existing experimental content is reorganized without new plots or table results.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical checkability through local proof and definition corrections, particularly the incomplete inverse Catoni definition. Corrected MDPR training formulas, added code-access information and clearer explanations also improve reproducibility and readability. These are useful, limited gains while the principal contributions and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
